name: Creator vlog
summary: A person talks to the lens in a room or on the move. Every pause is cut out, and a title, a sound or a cut-away lands every few seconds. The creator is the set, the brand and the grade.

philosophy.core_thesis: A direct address from one person, tightened by the jump cut, builds more trust than a produced film, so the creator's pace is the style.
design_principles: Frame the face at arm's length, 0.4 to 0.7 m, with a 16mm to 24mm lens (35mm format), in 16:9 at 24 or 30 fps, 180° shutter.
Hook inside the first 5 to 10 s with the promise of the video, and show the payoff before 30 s.
Cut out each pause longer than 0.3 s; keep an average shot length of 3 to 5 s with a jump cut or a punch-in of 10% to 20%.
Add a cut-away or a b-roll shot of 1 to 3 s every 6 to 10 s, and a text or a sound effect on each change of topic.
Light the face with a soft key at 45° and 5600K, at a key-to-fill ratio of 2:1, with a window or a panel at 1 m.
Record the voice at 0.3 m with a lavalier or a shotgun, mix at −14 LUFS integrated, and sit the music bed 18 to 24 dB below the voice.
Grade for warm, clean skin: saturation +10%, a gentle S-curve, a white balance of 5300K to 5600K.
anti_patterns: Long pauses and filler words left in
A tripod shot with a dead static frame for 60 s
A cinematic letterbox with a heavy teal grade
A voice recorded on the camera microphone at 3 m
A slow intro with a logo before the hook
A script read from a teleprompter with no eye contact

composition.framing: A close medium shot in 16:9, the face at 35% to 50% of the frame height, a wide-angle edge that bends the room.
composition.staging_in_depth: The face at 0.5 m, the room at 1 to 3 m behind it; the background is a lived-in room, not a set.
composition.subject_placement: Eyes on the upper third line, centred or off centre by up to 15%; the lens is the second person in the room.

principles.rule: Put the face on the upper third and fill the frame with it, so that the first frame is a person.
Look at the lens, not at the screen, for the direct address, and look away on the cut.
Remove every pause and breath with a jump cut so that the cut rate sets the pace.
Give the text card one size above all others and show it for the time of one read.
principles.value: 1 caption at a time, 1 to 2 s

principles.rule: Place the eyes on the upper third line and leave head room.
principles.value: eyes on the upper third line

camera_and_movement.movement: Handheld at arm's length or on a gimbal grip; the camera walks with the creator. Cut-aways are static or on a slow slider.
camera_and_movement.camera_height: At the eye or slightly above, 1.5 to 1.8 m
camera_and_movement.move_speed: Walking pace, 1.0 to 1.5 m/s; a punch-in of 10% to 20% in 0.2 s on the edit

lens_and_format.focus: Face-tracking autofocus on the eye; the background falls off softly at f/2.0.

light.quality: Soft: a window or an LED panel with a diffuser, and the room lamps as a warm practical.
light.direction: Key from 45° to the side and slightly above the eye line; a lamp in the background for depth.
light.source: Window, LED panel and room lamps

colour_and_grade.treatment: Clean, bright, warm skin. The grade is light and consistent from video to video, so the channel has one look.
grade_recipe: Set the black point at 3% and the white point at 97%; the image is bright and open.
Add a gentle S-curve of +10% contrast and keep skin at 60% to 75% luma.
Set white balance at 5300K to 5600K and nudge tint by +3 toward magenta for skin.
Raise saturation by +10% and lift the shadows by 4%.
Sharpen at 15%, add no grain and no vignette.

editing_and_rhythm.shot_length_range: 0.5 s for a sound-effect cut to 12 s for a story beat
editing_and_rhythm.cutting_logic: Remove each pause and breath; cut on the first word of the next phrase and punch in by 10% to 20% on a second angle.
editing_and_rhythm.transitions: Hard jump cut; a whoosh sound with a 4-frame zoom for a topic change; no dissolve.

sound.approach: The voice leads at all times. Add a sound effect on each text or topic change and a music bed that ducks under speech.
sound.dialogue: Direct address, 150 to 190 words per minute, in a casual register.
sound.music: A looped instrumental bed at 18 to 24 dB below the voice; a stronger cue for b-roll.

titles_and_graphics.treatment: A big, simple caption on key words, a lower third for 1.5 to 2 s, and a hand-drawn arrow or an emoji as a joke.
titles_and_graphics.type: Bold sans-serif at 5% to 8% of frame height, white with a 2 px dark outline; one accent colour.

shot_primer.opening: Open on the face, mid-sentence, with the hook line in the first 5 s and no logo.

positive: handheld selfie shot at arm's length

emotion.target_response: Closeness and a sense of company: the viewer feels a friend is talking, fast and honest.

use_cases: video prompts for a day-in-the-life clip
avoid_when: The brief needs a cinematic mood with no direct address.
The speaker has no personality to carry 8 to 15 min.

modifiers.how: Keep the direct address and the jump cut; move to 9:16, cut at 1.5 to 3 s and burn the captions in.
Keep the handheld address; move to 4:3 tape look at 25 or 30 fps with on-camera audio and a date stamp.

sources.title: Cinemetrics (Yuri Tsivian, University of Chicago): shot length statistics
Loudness reference: ITU-R BS.1770 and EBU R128 (levels in LUFS)
